title: Black Beans, Canned, Sodium Added, Drained and Rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Black beans in cans are cooked beans that have been harvested, cleaned, boiled, and sealed in a brine solution with added salt. After opening, they are typically drained and rinsed to reduce sodium content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans belong to the legume family and are also known as "turtle beans" or "black soybeans".
They are rich in antioxidants, especially anthocyanins, which give them their deep dark color.
Canning allows them to be stored for several years without significant loss of most nutrients.
Draining and rinsing canned beans can cut sodium levels by 40‑60 %.
Black beans are a staple in Latin American cuisine, featuring in dishes like feijoada and black bean soup.

items.title: High in plant protein
items.content: One cup (about 170 g) of canned black beans provides roughly 15 g of protein, beneficial for vegetarians and athletes.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport, while folate is important for DNA synthesis and cell growth.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Black beans raise blood glucose slowly, making them a good choice for people with diabetes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned beans can contain up to 400 mg of sodium per 100 g; draining and rinsing reduces it, but salt cannot be eliminated completely.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Bacterial contamination if improperly stored
items.content: Bulging or damaged cans may harbor pathogenic bacteria and should be discarded.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: After draining and rinsing, add black beans to salads, soups, chili, stews, mash them for spreads, or use as a filling for tacos. They also heat quickly in a skillet with vegetables and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3‑4 days.
